findings.title: Rule 16's operator action prescribes a re-drive of a terminally failed purge that no code path can perform
findings.reason: Round 3 re-resolved the clause this round CHANGED. The paragraph replaced 'no admin route mutates purge state' with a named exception: the teardown retry path is scoped to failed_step='teardown' - both AccountOffboardingTeardownRetryPoller and shouldTransitionToPurgeScheduled, the predicate behind the admin provider-disposition route (recordProviderDisposition); it is the one admin path that writes status/failed_step at all; on a failed_step='purge' row the predicate is false, so it records the disposition and leaves both untouched. All three halves resolve TRUE at fac1246: shouldTransitionToPurgeScheduled (src/lib/account-offboarding/provider-disposition.ts:277-295) returns false unless row.status='failed' (:281) AND row.failed_step='teardown' (:282); recordProviderDisposition's UPDATE (:183-191) sets status and failed_step to row.status and row.failed_step verbatim when the predicate is false (:179-180), so the stored values are unchanged; and src/app/api/admin/** contains exactly one route touching those columns - admin/offboardings/[offboardingId]/provider-disposition/route.ts. The other two library writers are OWNER routes, not admin: retry-billing.ts:67-82 (reachable only from /api/account/offboarding/retry-billing and scoped to mode='cancel_only' AND failed_step='billing') and keep-my-data.ts:181. The round-2 verification of the rest of the paragraph still holds; every production file it cites is byte-identical at fac1246. 'tracked in #1411' stays UNVERIFIABLE-EXTERNAL.

findings.title: The cell pins assert PRESENCE, not polarity: prefixing a facet with a negation leaves every assertion green while the row instructs the operator to do the opposite
findings.arbiter_reasoning: Measured three times, in three different cells of the same row, each as a single change against a green baseline, each SURVIVING. M11: the filter cell's 'filter tag terminal equals true AND level equals error' became 'do **not** filter tag terminal equals true AND level equals error'. M18: the trigger cell's 'Every event, action throttle 60 minutes per issue;' became 'Do **not** use Every event, and do **not** set the action throttle 60 minutes per issue;'. M19: the grouping cell's 'which is the whole grouping:' became 'which is NOT the grouping to configure:'. NOT EQUIVALENT: after M11 an operator following the row builds a Sentry rule with no terminal, level, subsystem or step filter at all, so every retry warning from alertPurgeFailure pages the Discord channel - the retry/terminal conflation this whole change exists to undo, one level further out, plus the loss of the environment and subsystem scoping. After M18 the rule is saved first-seen with no throttle, which is literally the RT-08 defect. NOT AN UNEXECUTED BRANCH: the mutated cells are the ones read at PurgeWorker.test.ts:967-969 and every assertion over them runs (M7, M12, M13, M14, M15 all kill inside these same cells). NOT CONTRIVED: the filter cell ALREADY contains a negated instruction in production prose - 'Do **not** filter on Sentry priority - CONFIG-1 established ...' - so prefixing a facet with 'do **not**' is a shape this cell natively takes, not an invented one. The pin is 17-for-24 against value corruption and 0-for-3 against polarity. Behavioural replacement, cheap: pin each facet as the whole clause it lives in rather than as a substring - require the filter cell to match a pattern anchored on the clause opener (start of cell, or a preceding '; ' / ', ') and to NOT match /do \*\*not\*\* filter tag/, and require the trigger cell to START with /^Every event, action throttle/. NOTE FOR THE ARBITER: this is a P0 by the skill's survivor rule and by operator impact, but it is NOT a claim that the test is worthless - it kills every VALUE corruption, including both the round-1 and the round-2 survivor. The owner may reasonably adjudicate it to accepted-risk on the ground that a regex pin over English prose cannot be made negation-proof without pinning whole sentences, which the row's own contract ('Nothing else in the row is pinned') deliberately refuses. That call is the owner's, not this pass's.

findings.title: stripComments treats comment markers inside string and regex literals as comments; the block-comment case blanks a multi-line SPAN and is not in the docblock's disclosure
findings.arbiter_reasoning: Four measured survivors of the single-owner test, all in one class. N2, N5 and N7 put a line-comment marker inside a string, inside a regex literal, and inside an https URL respectively, earlier on the same line as a respelled key, and the guard went blind to the key - exactly the imprecision ingest.test.ts:110-113 declares ('a `//` inside a string or regex literal is treated as a comment. That can only ever hide text AFTER the `//` on that line'). N9 is the one the docblock does NOT cover: a string holding an opening block-comment sequence, placed near the top of purge-stages.ts, opens a span that the non-greedy block pattern consumes all the way to the file's next real closing sequence, blanking every line in between - including the respelled key - so the blast radius is a multi-line SPAN, not a line tail. P2, and this is the same deliberate deviation from the skill's survivor-to-P0 mapping that round 2 declared for RT16-09, stated so it can be overruled: none of these four shapes is one production key construction takes, the change is a net INCREASE in guard strength over both the merge base and round 2 (N1, N3, N4, N6 and N8 all kill, and N1/N3 are the holes round 2 found), and the test's own comment already declares the guard is 'a regex over source text, not a dataflow analysis ... not a proof of single ownership'. Cheap hardening, if wanted: extend the docblock's disclosure to the block-comment-in-a-literal span case, which is the only part of this finding that is a documentation gap rather than an accepted scanner limit.

findings.title: rule16TableRow pins only the FIRST row matching the rule name, so a contradictory duplicate row below it is invisible
findings.arbiter_reasoning: Measured: M6a inserted a corrupted copy of the rule-16 row (terminal equals false, First seen) ABOVE the real one and the test FAILED; M6b inserted the same corrupted copy BELOW the real one and the test stayed GREEN, because rule16TableRow (PurgeWorker.test.ts:297-303) uses Array.prototype.find and stops at the first line in rule 16's block that starts with a pipe and contains the rule name. The runbook then carries two rows under one rule name giving opposite instructions, and the pin is silent about it. P2 rather than P0, declared as a deviation: unlike RT16-11 the configured row an operator would copy is still correct and still fully pinned, the mutation ADDS a contradictory row rather than inverting the authoritative one, and a duplicated rule-name row is not a shape an ordinary edit produces. Cheap hardening: filter instead of find and assert exactly one matching row, which also future-proofs rule16ColumnIndex's identical .find over the header row.

findings.title: 'Nothing else in the row is pinned' is false in the safe direction: the rule-name cell and the table's three column headers are pinned too
findings.arbiter_reasoning: Duty-3 re-resolution of a sentence this round ADDED. The runbook's rule-16 paragraph ends 'Nothing else in the row is pinned.' and .claude/reference/arch-review-log.md:3 repeats it as 'and nothing else in the row'. Measured counter-examples: M9 renamed the rule inside the row only and the test FAILED, because RULE_16_ROW_NAME (PurgeWorker.test.ts:276) is how rule16TableRow locates the row; M4 deleted the table header row and M5 reordered its columns, and both FAILED, because rule16ColumnIndex requires a header row carrying the exact strings 'Rule name', 'Emitted identity and filter', 'Level and grouping' and 'Trigger and destination'. Every facet-by-facet claim in the same sentence is EXACT (verified one by one against PurgeWorker.test.ts:970-1013: filter cell - terminal true, never false, level, subsystem, step, environment scoping; grouping cell - opening level plus both fingerprints position-scoped; trigger cell - every event, never first-seen, 60-minutes-per-issue throttle, integration 443670). P2, not P0: the statement UNDER-states what is pinned, so it can surprise an editor but can never give an operator false confidence that a value is protected when it is not - the direction a P0 doc claim fails in. Fix is one clause: '... and nothing else in the row, beyond the rule name and the column headers the cells are found by.'
